newsitem.title: USA: Comcast hurt by start-up costs, sells Nextel stake.
newsitem.headline: Comcast hurt by start-up costs, sells Nextel stake.

text.p: Comcast Corp. reported a second-quarter loss Monday due to various start-up costs and said it sold its remaining position in Nextel Communications Inc. last month for $73.4 million.
Nextel, a McLean, Va.-based provider of all-digital wireless services, also reported a loss for the second quarter.

Comcast, the Philadelphia-based cable television and telephone services company, held $300 million worth of stock in Nextel and began selling the shares in the second quarter. It sold its remaining stake of 3.3 million shares in July.
In the current year through July 31, Comcast said sales of non-strategic assets have generated more than $215 million in cash proceeds, which exceeded the company's investment by $138 million.
The company reported a loss for the second quarter of $37.4 million, or 12 cents a share, compared with a profit a year earlier of $16.8 million, or seven cents a share.

The loss was primarily attributable to start-up costs of various affiliates, principally Sprint PCS, a partnership building a nationwide personal communications service network in which Comcast has a 15 percent interest.
Revenues rose to $1.18 billion from $945 million.
Current year results include operations of Scripps cable properties, acquired in November, 1996, and E! Entertainment cable network, acquired in March, 1997.

Comcast is also the principal owner of QVC, the cable TV retailer. QVC's revenues increased 15.3 percent in the second quarter of 1997 to $467.7 million from the $405.7 million reported for the same period in 1996.
Comcast's Class A stock was unchanged at $23.4375 in midday trading on Nasdaq.
Nextel had a second-quarter loss of $261.6 million, or $1.08 a share, compared with a loss of $130.2 million, or 58 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $145.9 million from $77.6 million a year earlier.

Radio service revenue, which reflects airtime usage and monthly fees, increased 106 percent to $139.8 million for the quarter ended June 30, compared with $67.7 million for the same period last year, and 35 percent over first quarter's radio service revenue of $103.7 million.

Digital mobile units in service increased 255 percent to 624,400 from last year's second-quarter figure of 176,000 digital units in service, and 48 percent over the first quarter 1997 ending level of 422,900 digital units.
Monthly average revenue per digital unit increased to an average of approximately $63 for the current quarter, up from $59 during the first quarter.

During the quarter, Nextel "gained the support of our bondholders for a more aggressive network buildout plan. Since the end of the quarter, Nextel has been able to obtain approximately $1 billion in new equity investment and debt financing commitments," said Steve Shindler, Nextel's chief financial officer.

The new funding sources include $232.5 million in new equity from the McCaw Family, the issuance of $500 million in Series D exchangeable preferred stock and the receipt of commitments for $250 million in a senior secured term loan, the company said.
Nextel stock fell $1.125 to $23.8125 in midday trading on Nasdaq.
